name: The Long View
tagline: The worse it gets, the clearer you are.
epigraph: Rye and orange, after a bartender whose book came out as the ban ended.
glassware: stemmed sour glass (about 240 ml), chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's checks on v3: history about 48% of yours (196 of 412 words); every paragraph, the title block and the closing line clean on 4-grams against every pour and the registry (B2 reworded to "head bartender of New York's Ashland House" after "head bartender at the" hit *As It Was* and *One Table*). Every "he", "him" or "his" in yours 1–4 is Duffy (lint warnings accepted by Wren, r5). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/patrick-gavin-duffy.md`. Oxford Companion: DUFFY, PATRICK GAVIN (pdf 687–688, Stailey), primary; *Imbibe!* pdf 91–92 (Wondrich), primary; *Joy* pdf 63, 348 (date check). Web: two newspaper visits for the 1 December 1933 *Brooklyn Eagle* interview (OCR kept in `work/ruler-magician/historian-evidence-duffy-1933-press-ocr.txt`), which settles the year as 1933; both web visits spent. The 1933 *Manual* itself isn't in the library.
names_note: *The Long View* (all three, round 5: Tomás's pick; Wren moved from *The Quiet Years*, Hester from *Days Early*), over *Seen Coming* and *Before Anyone Asked*. No crossing: the voices held their picks until round 5.
open_items: F16 (same 1933 interview: Duffy disapproved of women bartenders and mixed drinking, and called liquor a heart spur in sickness) stays in the dossier only, never told, by Wren's ruling; Robin to confirm it stays out.
The 1933 *Official Mixer's Manual* isn't in the library: the Herald Punch recipe rests on Wondrich's reading of it.
One unsourced value: the lightly aged St. Croix rum style.
